exercises.name: Downward-Facing Dog
instructions: Start on your hands and knees with wrists under shoulders and knees under hips.
Tuck your toes and lift your hips up and back toward the ceiling.
Straighten your legs and press your heels toward the floor.
Spread your fingers wide and press your palms into the mat.
Hold the position while breathing deeply, keeping your head between your arms.
exercises.overview: A foundational yoga pose that stretches the hamstrings, calves, and shoulders while strengthening the upper body.

exercises.name: Seated Forward Fold
instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended straight in front of you.
Flex your feet toward your shins.
Hinge at your hips and reach your hands toward your toes.
Keep your spine as straight as possible rather than rounding your back.
Hold the stretch while breathing deeply into the back of your legs.
exercises.overview: A seated hamstring stretch that improves flexibility in the posterior chain and lower back.

exercises.name: Pigeon Pose
instructions: Start in a high plank position and bring your right knee forward behind your right wrist.
Extend your left leg straight behind you, keeping your hips square.
Lower your upper body toward the floor, resting on your forearms.
Hold the position and breathe deeply into your right hip.
Repeat on the left side for the same duration.
exercises.overview: A deep hip opener that targets the glutes, piriformis, and hip flexors for improved hip mobility.

exercises.name: Cat-Cow Stretch
instructions: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Inhale and arch your back, lifting your chest and tailbone (Cow pose).
Exhale and round your spine, tucking your chin to your chest (Cat pose).
Continue alternating between Cat and Cow with your breath.
Perform 10 complete cycles for a thorough spinal mobilization.
exercises.overview: A dynamic spinal mobility exercise that alternates between flexion and extension to warm up the spine.

exercises.name: Standing Quad Stretch
instructions: Stand tall with feet hip-width apart.
Bend your right knee and grab your right ankle with your right hand.
Pull your heel toward your glutes, keeping your knees together.
Keep your torso upright and push your hips slightly forward.
Hold the stretch and repeat on the left side.
exercises.overview: A basic standing stretch targeting the quadriceps and hip flexors for improved leg flexibility.

exercises.name: Lying Figure-Four Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with your knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Cross your right ankle over your left knee, forming a figure-four shape.
Reach through and grab the back of your left thigh, pulling it toward your chest.
Hold the stretch and feel it in your right glute and hip.
Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.overview: A supine glute stretch using the figure-four position to target the piriformis and external hip rotators.

exercises.name: Cobra Pose
instructions: Lie face down on your mat with your hands under your shoulders.
Press your hands into the mat to lift your upper body off the floor.
Keep your hips on the mat and your elbows slightly bent.
Open your chest and look slightly upward.
Hold the position while breathing deeply.
exercises.overview: A yoga backbend that stretches the abdominals, hip flexors, and chest while strengthening the spine.

exercises.name: Foam Rolling - IT Band
instructions: Lie on your side with the foam roller under your outer thigh, just below your hip.
Support your upper body on your forearm.
Slowly roll along the outside of your thigh from hip to just above the knee.
Pause on any tender spots for 10-15 seconds.
Avoid rolling directly over the knee joint.
exercises.overview: A self-myofascial release technique targeting the IT band and tensor fasciae latae for improved leg recovery and flexibility.

exercises.name: Foam Rolling - Upper Back
instructions: Lie on your back with the foam roller positioned under your mid-back.
Bend your knees with feet flat on the floor for support.
Cross your arms over your chest to expose your shoulder blades.
Roll slowly from your mid-back to your upper back.
Pause on any tender spots and breathe deeply.
exercises.overview: A foam rolling exercise for the upper back that releases tension in the rhomboids, traps, and spinal erectors.

exercises.name: World's Greatest Stretch
instructions: Start in a lunge position with your right foot forward.
Place your right hand on the ground beside your right foot.
Rotate your left arm toward the ceiling, opening your chest and looking up.
Return your left hand to the ground and straighten your right leg, lifting your hips.
Step back to a plank and repeat on the left side.
exercises.overview: A dynamic mobility exercise that combines a lunge, thoracic rotation, and hip flexor stretch for comprehensive warm-up.

exercises.name: 90/90 Hip Stretch
instructions: Sit on the floor with your front leg bent at 90 degrees in front of you.
Your back leg should also be bent at 90 degrees behind you.
Keep both knees at 90-degree angles — your front shin is parallel, back shin is perpendicular.
Slowly lean your torso forward over your front shin.
Hold and repeat on the other side.
exercises.overview: A seated hip mobility stretch targeting both internal and external hip rotation for comprehensive hip flexibility.

exercises.name: Band-Assisted Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Lie on your back with a resistance band looped around your right foot.
Hold both ends of the band with your hands.
Keeping your left leg flat on the ground, use the band to pull your right leg toward you.
Keep your right knee straight and your foot flexed.
Hold at the point of comfortable stretch.
exercises.overview: A band-assisted hamstring stretch using PNF principles for improved flexibility through gradual range of motion increases.

exercises.name: Wrist Flexor Stretch
instructions: Extend your right arm in front of you with your palm facing up.
Use your left hand to gently pull your right fingers back toward your body.
Keep your right elbow straight throughout the stretch.
Hold the stretch and feel it along the underside of your forearm.
Repeat on the left side.
exercises.overview: A wrist flexor stretch to improve forearm flexibility and prevent wrist-related injuries from lifting.

exercises.name: Neck Flexion Stretch
instructions: Sit or stand tall with your shoulders relaxed.
Tilt your right ear toward your right shoulder, keeping your shoulders down.
You can use your right hand to gently apply extra pressure.
Hold the stretch on the left side of your neck.
Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.overview: A simple neck stretch that targets the upper trapezius and levator scapulae to relieve neck tension.

exercises.name: Ankle Circles
instructions: Sit or stand with one foot lifted slightly off the ground.
Slowly rotate your ankle in a clockwise direction, making large circles.
Complete 10 full rotations.
Reverse direction and rotate counterclockwise for 10 more.
Repeat on the opposite ankle.
exercises.overview: A simple ankle mobility exercise that improves dorsiflexion and ankle stability for better movement quality.

exercises.name: Thread the Needle
instructions: Start on your hands and knees in a tabletop position.
Reach your right arm under your body and toward the left side, threading it through.
Lower your right shoulder and ear to the mat.
Hold the position, breathing deeply to allow your thoracic spine to rotate.
Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.overview: A thoracic spine rotation stretch that improves mid-back mobility and releases tension between the shoulder blades.

exercises.name: Shoulder Cross-Body Stretch
instructions: Stand tall and bring your right arm across your body at chest height.
Use your left hand to gently pull your right arm closer to your chest.
Keep your right shoulder relaxed and down.
Hold the stretch in the back of your right shoulder.
Repeat on the opposite side.
exercises.overview: A simple shoulder stretch targeting the rear deltoid and posterior capsule for improved shoulder mobility.

exercises.name: Standing Straddle Stretch
instructions: Stand with your feet wider than shoulder-width apart, toes pointing forward.
Hinge at your hips and lower your torso toward the floor.
Reach your hands toward the ground or grab your ankles.
Keep your legs as straight as possible.
Hold the stretch and breathe deeply.
exercises.overview: A standing groin and hamstring stretch using a wide straddle position for inner thigh flexibility.

exercises.name: Jefferson Curl
instructions: Stand on an elevated surface (step or plates) with a light barbell.
Hold the bar with a shoulder-width overhand grip.
Slowly curl your spine forward, vertebra by vertebra, lowering the bar along your legs.
Lower as far as comfortable while keeping your legs straight.
Reverse the motion slowly, uncurling your spine one vertebra at a time.
exercises.overview: An advanced loaded stretch that progressively increases hamstring and spinal flexibility under light resistance.

exercises.name: Tabata Bodyweight Squats
instructions: Set a timer for 8 rounds of 20 seconds work and 10 seconds rest.
Stand with feet shoulder-width apart.
Perform as many bodyweight squats as possible in 20 seconds.
Rest for 10 seconds.
Repeat for a total of 8 rounds (4 minutes total).
exercises.overview: A Tabata protocol bodyweight squat workout providing high-intensity interval training in just 4 minutes.

exercises.name: Tabata Push-Ups
instructions: Set a timer for 8 rounds of 20 seconds work and 10 seconds rest.
Start in a high plank position with hands under shoulders.
Perform as many push-ups as possible with proper form in 20 seconds.
Rest for 10 seconds in plank or downward dog.
Complete all 8 rounds (4 minutes total).
exercises.overview: A Tabata push-up protocol that builds upper body muscular endurance and cardiovascular fitness in 4 minutes.

exercises.name: Burpee to Pull-Up
instructions: Stand under a pull-up bar.
Drop into a squat, place your hands on the floor, and kick your feet back into a plank.
Perform a push-up, then jump your feet forward to a squat.
Jump up and grab the pull-up bar.
Perform one pull-up, release, and land softly.
exercises.overview: An advanced compound movement combining a burpee with a pull-up for maximum full-body conditioning.

exercises.name: Battle Rope Waves
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding one end of each rope.
Bend your knees slightly and brace your core.
Alternately raise and lower each arm to create waves in the ropes.
Maintain a fast, consistent pace throughout the work interval.
Rest for 30 seconds between sets.
exercises.overview: A high-intensity battle rope exercise that builds shoulder endurance, core stability, and cardiovascular fitness simultaneously.

exercises.name: EMOM Thrusters
instructions: Load a barbell with moderate weight.
At the start of every minute (EMOM), perform 10 thrusters.
A thruster is a front squat followed immediately by an overhead press.
Rest for the remaining time in the minute.
Complete 10 rounds total.
exercises.overview: An Every Minute On the Minute (EMOM) thruster workout that builds full-body power and cardiovascular endurance.

exercises.name: Sprint Intervals
instructions: Find a flat surface or track with at least 50 meters of clear space.
Sprint at maximum effort for 30 seconds.
Walk or jog slowly for 60 seconds to recover.
Repeat the sprint-recovery cycle for 8 rounds.
Cool down with a 5-minute easy jog.
exercises.overview: Short sprint intervals that maximize anaerobic capacity, calorie burn, and cardiovascular fitness in minimal time.

exercises.name: Box Jump Overs
instructions: Stand facing a plyo box at arm's length distance.
Swing your arms and jump up onto the box, landing softly with both feet.
Instead of stepping down, jump over the box to the other side.
Immediately turn around and jump back over the box.
Continue jumping back and forth for the prescribed reps.
exercises.overview: A continuous box jump exercise that adds a lateral jump-over component for increased intensity and conditioning.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Slams
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart holding a medicine ball overhead.
Explosively slam the ball into the ground in front of you.
Bend your knees slightly and pick up the ball.
Lift it back overhead and slam it again.
Maintain a fast, aggressive pace throughout the set.
exercises.overview: An explosive full-body exercise using a medicine ball slam for power development and cardiovascular conditioning.

exercises.name: Depth Jump
instructions: Stand on a plyo box that is 12-18 inches high.
Step off the box (do not jump) and land on both feet.
Upon landing, immediately jump as high as possible vertically.
Minimize ground contact time between landing and jumping.
Land softly on the floor and step back onto the box.
exercises.overview: An advanced plyometric exercise that develops reactive strength by using the stretch-shortening cycle from a drop landing.

exercises.name: Lateral Bounds
instructions: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart in an athletic stance.
Jump laterally to your right as far as possible, landing on your right foot.
Immediately push off and bound back to the left, landing on your left foot.
Use your arms to help generate power.
Keep your landings soft and controlled.
exercises.overview: A lateral plyometric exercise that develops explosive side-to-side power and hip stability.

instructions: Start in a standard push-up position with hands slightly wider than shoulders.
Lower into a push-up with controlled speed.
Explosively push up so your hands leave the ground.
Clap your hands together quickly while in the air.
Land with soft elbows and immediately lower into the next rep.
exercises.overview: An explosive push-up variation where you clap your hands in mid-air, developing upper body power and speed.

exercises.name: Medicine Ball Chest Pass
instructions: Stand facing a wall or partner, 3-4 feet away.
Hold a medicine ball at chest level with both hands.
Step forward with one foot and explosively push the ball forward.
Catch the rebound (or have partner pass it back).
Immediately repeat the chest pass.
exercises.overview: An explosive medicine ball exercise that develops pushing power and upper body speed through repeated chest passes.

instructions: Start in a sprint stance.
Drive your right knee up and forward while extending your left leg behind you.
Cover as much ground as possible with each stride.
Focus on long, powerful strides with maximum hang time.
Alternate legs in an exaggerated running motion for the prescribed distance.
exercises.overview: An exaggerated running exercise that develops stride power, hip extension force, and sprint mechanics.

exercises.name: Skater Jumps
instructions: Stand with your feet together.
Jump laterally to your right, landing on your right foot while sweeping your left foot behind you.
Immediately jump laterally to your left, landing on your left foot.
Continue alternating sides in a skating motion.
Land softly on each jump and maintain your balance.
exercises.overview: A lateral plyometric exercise mimicking a skating motion to build lateral power, agility, and single-leg stability.

instructions: Stand on one leg facing a low plyo box.
Swing your arms and jump up onto the box using only one leg.
Land softly on the box with the same foot.
Step down carefully and reset before the next jump.
Complete all reps on one leg before switching.
exercises.overview: An advanced unilateral plyometric exercise that develops single-leg explosive power and ankle stability.

instructions: Stand perpendicular to a wall, 3 feet away, holding a medicine ball at waist level.
Rotate your torso away from the wall, loading your hips.
Explosively rotate toward the wall and throw the medicine ball.
Catch the rebound and immediately rotate away again.
Complete all reps on one side before switching.
exercises.overview: A rotational medicine ball throw that develops rotational power for sports performance and core strength.

instructions: Pick up a heavy dumbbell or kettlebell in each hand.
Stand tall with shoulders back and core braced.
Walk forward with short, quick steps while maintaining an upright posture.
Keep the weights at your sides — do not swing them.
Walk the prescribed distance or time while maintaining grip.
exercises.overview: A loaded carry exercise that builds total body strength, grip endurance, and core stability simultaneously.

instructions: Start on all fours with your hands under shoulders and knees under hips.
Lift your knees 1-2 inches off the ground (bear position).
Crawl forward by moving your right hand and left foot simultaneously.
Then move your left hand and right foot.
Keep your hips low and core engaged throughout.
exercises.overview: A crawling exercise that builds full-body strength, coordination, and cardiovascular conditioning through primal movement patterns.

instructions: Load a sled with appropriate weight.
Stand behind the sled with hands on the handles at chest height.
Lean into the sled and drive forward by pushing with your legs.
Keep your core tight and take powerful, short strides.
Push the sled the prescribed distance.
exercises.overview: A heavy sled push that develops leg drive, full-body power, and anaerobic conditioning.

instructions: Lie on your back holding a kettlebell straight up with your right hand.
Bend your right knee and place your left arm out to the side.
Roll up onto your left elbow, then your left hand.
Bridge your hips, sweep your left leg back, and come to a half-kneeling position.
Stand up while keeping the kettlebell locked out overhead. Reverse the steps.
exercises.overview: A full-body kettlebell exercise that builds shoulder stability, core strength, and hip mobility through a multi-step movement.

instructions: Sit on the floor with your knees bent and feet flat.
Place your hands behind you with fingers pointing toward your feet.
Lift your hips off the floor.
Walk forward on your hands and feet simultaneously.
Keep your hips elevated throughout the movement.
exercises.overview: A bodyweight crawling exercise that strengthens the posterior chain, triceps, and shoulders while improving mobility.

instructions: Stand at the base of the climbing rope and grip it with both hands.
Jump up slightly and wrap the rope between your feet.
Pull yourself up by alternating your grip (hand over hand).
Use your feet to squeeze the rope for assistance.
Climb to the top, then descend slowly and under control.
exercises.overview: An advanced climbing exercise that builds extraordinary upper body strength, grip endurance, and full-body coordination.

instructions: Lie on your back with a resistance band above your knees.
Bend your knees with feet flat on the floor.
Lift one leg off the ground, extending it straight.
Push through the heel of your grounded foot to lift your hips.
Squeeze your glutes at the top and slowly lower back down.
exercises.overview: A banded single-leg glute bridge that targets glute activation for rehabilitation and injury prevention.

instructions: Stand with your back against a wall.
Place your forearms against the wall with elbows at 90 degrees.
Slide your arms up the wall as high as comfortable without arching your back.
Pull your forearms back down to the starting position.
Keep your back and wrists flat against the wall throughout.
exercises.overview: A scapular wall slide exercise that strengthens the lower trapezius and serratus anterior for shoulder health and posture.

instructions: Stand tall holding a resistance band in front of your chest with both hands.
Grip the band at shoulder width with palms facing down.
Pull the band apart by squeezing your shoulder blades together.
Stretch the band until it touches your chest.
Slowly return to the starting position with control.
exercises.overview: A simple resistance band exercise that strengthens the rear deltoids and rotator cuff for shoulder health and posture.

instructions: Start in a standard plank position with arms straight.
Keep your elbows locked and lower your body slightly by protracting your shoulder blades.
Push your body back up by squeezing your shoulder blades together (retracting).
The range of motion is small — only 1-2 inches.
Focus on moving through the shoulder blades, not the elbows.
exercises.overview: A push-up variation that isolates scapular movement to strengthen the serratus anterior and improve shoulder mechanics.

instructions: Sit on the floor with your legs extended.
Loop a resistance band around one foot and anchor it to a sturdy object.
Pull your toes toward your shin (dorsiflexion) against the band resistance.
Hold for 2 seconds at the peak of the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.overview: A band-resisted ankle dorsiflexion exercise that strengthens the tibialis anterior and improves ankle mobility for injury prevention.

exercises: rotator Cuff External Rotation with Band
instructions: Stand with your elbow tucked against your side at 90 degrees.
Hold one end of a resistance band with your working hand, the other end anchored.
Rotate your forearm outward (away from your body) against the band resistance.
Keep your elbow pinned to your side throughout the movement.
Slowly return to the starting position.
exercises.overview: A band-resisted external rotation exercise that targets the rotator cuff muscles for shoulder health and injury prevention.

instructions: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor.
Lift your hips into a bridge position, squeezing your glutes.
While holding the bridge, lift one knee toward your chest.
Lower that foot and repeat with the other leg.
Keep your hips level and elevated throughout the marching motion.
exercises.overview: A glute bridge variation with alternating knee drives that challenges core stability while strengthening the glutes.

instructions: Lie face down on a mat with your arms extended overhead (Y position).
Lift your arms off the ground, squeezing your shoulder blades down and together.
Lower and move your arms to a T position (straight out to the sides), then lift.
Lower and move your arms to a W position (elbows bent at 90 degrees), then lift.
Perform 8 reps at each position.
exercises.overview: A comprehensive scapular strengthening exercise using Y, T, and W positions to target the lower and mid trapezius for posture correction.

instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar or rings with a false grip.
Perform an explosive pull-up, driving your chest above the bar/rings.
Transition your body over the bar/rings by shifting your weight forward.
Push up to full arm extension on top of the bar/rings.
Lower yourself back down with control.
exercises.overview: An advanced calisthenics movement combining a pull-up and dip for a complete upper body exercise on bars or rings.

instructions: Place your hands on parallettes or dip bars beside your hips.
Press down to lift your entire body off the ground.
Extend both legs straight out in front of you, parallel to the floor.
Hold this position while keeping your body as upright as possible.
Lower back down and rest before repeating.
exercises.overview: An advanced isometric hold on parallettes that requires extreme core, tricep, and shoulder strength.

instructions: Face a wall and place your hands on the floor 6 inches from the baseboard.
Kick up into a handstand with your back against the wall.
Lock out your arms and look at your hands.
Engage your core and squeeze your legs together.
Hold the position for the prescribed time.
exercises.overview: A freestanding or wall-assisted handstand that builds shoulder strength, balance, and body awareness.

instructions: Stand on one leg with the other leg extended in front of you.
Extend both arms forward for counterbalance.
Lower into a single-leg squat, keeping your raised leg off the ground.
Go as deep as possible while maintaining balance.
Drive through your heel to return to standing.
exercises.overview: An advanced single-leg bodyweight squat that requires exceptional leg strength, balance, and mobility.

instructions: Hang from a pull-up bar with an overhand grip.
Raise your legs until your body is horizontal and parallel to the ground.
Keep your body straight from head to toes.
Hold the position, squeezing your lats and core.
Lower back down with control.
exercises.overview: An advanced gymnastics hold on a pull-up bar that develops extraordinary back and core strength.
